chapters.title: 1. 아버지를 부를 수 없는 아이
chapters.text:
옛날에 홍 판서라는 사람이 살았다. 홍 판서는 나라의 중요한 일을 하는 사람이었다. 많은 사람들이 그를 알고 있었다.

홍 판서에게는 두 아들이 있었다. 첫째 아들은 홍인형이었다. 인형의 어머니는 홍 판서의 아내인 유 부인이었다. 둘째 아들은 홍길동이었다. 길동의 어머니는 춘섬이었다. 춘섬은 홍 판서의 집에서 일하는 여자였다. 두 아이는 아버지가 같았지만 어머니는 달랐다.

길동이 태어나기 전에 홍 판서는 특별한 꿈을 꾸었다. 꿈속에서 갑자기 큰 소리가 났다. 파란 용이 홍 판서에게 빨리 왔다. 홍 판서는 깜짝 놀라서 잠에서 깼다. 꿈이었다. 홍 판서는 그것을 알고 매우 기뻤다.

‘용이 나오는 꿈을 꾸었다. 특별한 아이가 태어날 것 같다.’

그 후 춘섬은 홍 판서와 함께 살게 되었다. 유 부인은 여전히 홍 판서의 아내였지만, 춘섬도 그의 가족이 되었다. 그리고 춘섬이 아들을 낳았다. 그 아이가 길동이었다. 길동은 보통 아기와는 모습이 달랐다. 홍 판서는 아들을 보고 기뻤다. 하지만 유 부인이 낳은 아들이 아니라서 슬픈 마음도 있었다.

길동은 자라서 여덟 살이 되었다. 아주 똑똑해서 하나를 배우면 다른 것도 많이 알 수 있었다. 홍 판서는 그런 길동을 더욱 사랑했다.

그러나 길동에게는 부를 수 없는 말이 있었다. 자기 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없었다. 인형도 자기 형이었지만 ‘형’이라고 부를 수 없었다. 그렇게 부르면 아버지는 길동을 혼냈다.

길동의 어머니 춘섬은 신분이 낮았기 때문이다. 그 사회에는 높은 신분의 사람과 낮은 신분의 사람이 있었다. 어머니의 신분이 낮으면 아이의 신분도 낮았다. 길동은 홍 판서의 아들이었지만, 어머니의 신분 때문에 인형과 똑같이 살 수 없었다.

길동은 열 살이 넘었지만 여전히 아버지와 형을 그렇게 부르지 못했다. 집에서 일하는 사람들까지 길동을 낮게 보았다. 길동은 너무 슬프고 마음이 아팠다.

어느 가을밤이었다. 달이 밝았다. 길동은 글을 읽다가 책상을 밀고 한숨을 쉬었다.

“나는 나라를 위해 중요한 일을 하고 싶다. 내 이름을 많은 사람들이 오래 기억하면 좋겠다. 그런데 나는 왜 이렇게 혼자일까? 아버지도 있고 형도 있는데 아버지와 형이라고 부르지 못한다. 마음이 너무 아프다.”

길동은 말을 마치고 밖으로 나갔다. 그리고 마당에서 칼을 쓰는 연습을 했다.

홍 판서도 밖에서 달을 보고 있었다. 그는 길동을 보고 가까이 불렀다.

“밤이 이렇게 늦었는데 왜 아직 잠을 안 자?”

길동은 아버지께 대답했다.

“달이 밝아서 보고 있었습니다. 그런데 사람은 모두 중요하지요. 왜 저는 중요한 사람이 아닌 것 같을까요?”

홍 판서는 길동의 말을 이해했다. 하지만 일부러 길동을 혼내면서 물었다.

“그게 무슨 말이야?”

길동은 아버지 앞에서 다시 절을 하고 말했다.

“저를 낳고 길러 주신 부모님께 감사합니다. 저는 아버지의 아들입니다. 하지만 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부르지 못합니다. 제 형도 ‘형’이라고 부르지 못합니다. 이것이 늘 슬픕니다. 저도 사람인데 왜 이렇게 살아야 합니까?”

길동은 눈물을 흘렸다. 눈물에 옷이 젖었다.

홍 판서도 길동이 불쌍했다. 그러나 길동에게 따뜻한 말을 해 주는 것이 걱정이었다. 길동이 자기 신분을 잊을 것 같았다. 그러면 자기 신분으로 할 수 없는 일까지 하려고 할 것 같았다. 그래서 큰 소리로 길동을 혼냈다.

“높은 사람의 집에서 일하는 여자가 낳은 아들은 너 말고도 있다. 너도 그런 아들인데 왜 이런 말을 해? 다시는 이런 말을 하지 마라. 또 이런 말을 하면 내 앞에 오지 못할 것이다.”

길동은 아무 말도 할 수 없었다. 그저 아버지 앞에 몸을 숙이고 울었다.

“이제 가라.”

홍 판서가 말했다. 길동은 자기 방으로 돌아갔다. 방에 돌아와서도 길동은 계속 슬펐다.

grammar_links.context_en: 에 marks 옛날 as the time when Minister Hong lived.
라는 modifies the following 사람, identifying him by the surname and title 홍 판서.
이 marks the person called Minister Hong as the subject of 살았다.
-았- places his life in the past, matching 옛날에.
-다 closes this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
는 establishes Minister Hong as the topic: the sentence explains his role.
의 connects the country to its important work or affairs.
중요한 describes 일 as important.
을 marks the important work as what Minister Hong did.
하는 modifies 사람: a person who did the country's important work. The activity is habitual relative to the past narration, rather than a completed action preceding it.
이다 connects Minister Hong to the description 사람, a person with this role.
었 places his described role in the past: he was such a person.
다 ends the past copular statement in the plain written narrative register.
많은 modifies 사람들이, describing a large number of people.
들 makes the plurality of 사람 explicit.
이 marks the people as those who knew Minister Hong.
를 marks Minister Hong, referred to as 그, as the person they knew.
-고 links 알다 to the auxiliary 있다. The following 있었다 places their knowledge at the past narrative moment.
With 알다, -고 있다 expresses a continuing state of knowing. 알고 있었다 means that the people knew Minister Hong at that past time.
-었- in 있었다 places the continuing state expressed by the auxiliary in the past.
-다 ends 있었다 as a plain narrative statement about that past state.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: were in that continuing state of knowing him

grammar_links.context_en: 에게 identifies Minister Hong as the person who had the two sons.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic of the statement and follows 에게.
이 marks the two sons as what Minister Hong had. The sentence means 'Minister Hong had two sons.'
-었- places Minister Hong's having two sons in the past.
-다 closes the past-tense predicate as a plain narrative statement.
은 marks the first son as the topic whose identity is given.
The copula identifies the first son as Hong Inhyeong.
The past marker places this identification in the time of the narrative.
Final -다 ends this past-tense identification in the chapter's plain narrative style.
의 identifies Inhyeong as the child of the mother being discussed. The shortened name retains Hong Inhyeong's full-name identity.
는 makes Inhyeong's mother the topic: the sentence identifies who she was.
의 connects Minister Hong to 아내: she was his wife.
인 makes 아내 identify Lady Yu as Minister Hong's wife. The past narration supplies the English past time.
The copula identifies Inhyeong's mother as Lady Yu.
었 places this identification in the past narrative: she was Lady Yu.
다 ends the identification as a plain narrative statement. It is included in the complete past copular form rather than shown as an additional transformation stage.
은 marks the second son as the topic, contrasting him with the first son introduced earlier.
The copula identifies the second son as Hong Gildong.
The past marker places this identification in the story's past narrative.
다 finishes the past identification as a plain narrative statement.
의 connects Gildong to his mother: ‘Gildong's mother’.
는 marks Gildong's mother as the topic whose identity is given.
The copula identifies Gildong's mother as Chunseom.
이었 places this identification in the past narrative: ‘was Chunseom’.
Final 다 closes the identification in plain written narration.
은 sets Chunseom as the topic of the description.
의 connects Minister Hong to his household.
에서 marks Minister Hong's household as the place where Chunseom worked.
일하는 describes 여자 by her work. Its time is relative to the past narration: she worked in the household.
The copula identifies Chunseom as a woman described by the preceding modifier.
였, contracted from 이었, places this description of Chunseom in the past.
Final -다 closes the past copular statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
는 makes the two children the topic. 두 supplies the plural meaning.
가 marks the father as the subject of 'was the same': the children shared one father.
-았- marks the shared parentage as a state in the past narrative. 같았다 is the complete plain statement form; the occurrence uses -지만 instead of the statement ending.
-지만 contrasts having the same father with having different mothers, retaining the past marking.
는 introduces their mothers as the contrasting topic: each child had a different mother.
The past form of 다르다 is 달랐다: 르 changes to ㄹ라 before -았-, and the complete form means 'were different' here.
-다 ends the past descriptive predicate as a plain narrative statement. This ending is already included in the complete past form.
이 marks Gildong as the person whose birth is mentioned in the before-clause.
-기 turns 태어나다 into an expression referring to being born, used before 전에.
The complete phrase places Minister Hong's dream before Gildong's birth.
에 follows 전 to mark the earlier time: before Gildong was born.
는 introduces Minister Hong as the topic of the main statement.
-ㄴ makes 특별하다 describe the following noun 꿈: a special dream.
을 marks 꿈 as the dream Minister Hong had; 꿈을 꾸다 means to dream.
-었- places Minister Hong's dreaming in the past.
-다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
에서 marks the dream as the setting where the sound rang out.
큰 modifies 소리. Here 크다 describes the loudness of a sound.
가 marks 소리 as the subject: the sound that rang out.
나- and -았- contract to 났-. The past marker places the sound's occurrence in the past; 소리가 나다 means that a sound is produced or heard.
-다 ends the past predicate as a plain statement in written narration.
파란 describes the dragon as blue. 파랗- + -ㄴ → 파란 drops ㅎ without changing the vowel.
이 marks the dragon as the subject: it is the dragon that came.
에게 marks Minister Hong as the person toward whom the dragon came.
왔다 places the dragon's arrival in the past.
The final -다 ends this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative style.
는 presents Minister Hong as the topic of the sentence.
-아서 connects his sudden fright to waking up. The final past predicate supplies the past time for this connective as well.
에서 marks sleep as the state he emerges from when he wakes.
In 깼다, 깨- combines with past -었- and contracts to 깼- before the statement ending -다. The complete form means ‘woke up’.
The ending -다 completes 깼다 as a plain narrative statement about his waking up.
Identifies what Minister Hong experienced as a dream.
Places the dream before his awakening.
Ends the narrator's statement in the plain written style.
는 marks Minister Hong as the topic: the sentence describes his reaction to the dream.
을 marks what he realized: that what he had experienced was a dream.
-고 connects his realization with his happiness. The following past predicate places both in the past.
기쁘다 becomes 기뻤다, placing his happiness in the past; the stem vowel ㅡ drops when the past ending is added.
-다 closes the past-tense description in the chapter's plain narrative register.
이 marks the dragon as the subject of 나오는: the dragon appears in the dream.
나오는 modifies 꿈: a dream in which a dragon appears. The appearance occurs within the dream, rather than at the speaker's present time.
을 marks 꿈 as the object of 꾸었다. 꿈을 꾸다 means to have a dream during sleep.
-었- places the dreaming in the past: Minister Hong says that he had a dream.
-다 ends this past statement in plain speech, appropriate to Minister Hong's private thought.
특별한 describes the following child as special.
가 marks the child as the subject of being born.
태어날 modifies 것 and presents the birth as an expected future event.
태어날 것 같다 expresses Minister Hong's expectation that a child will be born, rather than a certain prediction.
같다 ends the thought with a plain statement.
은 makes Chunseom the topic of the statement about her changed living circumstances.
와 marks Minister Hong as the person Chunseom lived with; 함께 reinforces the meaning ‘together’.
-게 connects 살다 to 되다, which expresses the change in Chunseom's circumstances.
살게 되었다 says that Chunseom came to live with Minister Hong as her circumstances changed.
-었- places the change in living circumstances in the past.
-다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
은 makes Lady Yu the topic and contrasts her continuing position as wife with Chunseom joining the family.
의 connects Minister Hong to his wife.
The copula identifies Lady Yu as Minister Hong's wife.
였 places Lady Yu's position as wife in the past narrative; 여전히 indicates that it continued.
지만 contrasts Lady Yu remaining his wife with Chunseom also becoming part of his family.
도 means that Chunseom also joined Minister Hong's family.
의 makes 그 possessive: his, referring to Minister Hong.
이 marks 가족 as the relationship Chunseom came to have: she became a member of his family.
었 marks Chunseom's becoming part of the family as a past event.
다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
이 marks Chunseom as the person who gave birth.
을 marks 아들 as the child Chunseom gave birth to.
-았- places the birth in the past; 낳다 becomes 낳았다 in this plain narrative statement.
Final -다 closes the past-tense predicate in the chapter's plain narrative register.
가 marks the child as the subject being identified as Gildong.
The copula identifies the child as Gildong using the approved shortened name 길동.
었 places the identification in the narrative past: the child was Gildong.
다 closes the past identification as a plain narrative statement.
은 establishes Gildong as the topic of the description.
와 marks a baby as the comparison partner for 달랐다; 보통 specifies an ordinary baby.
는 follows 와 to emphasize the contrast with an ordinary baby.
이 marks his appearance as what was different.
달랐다 describes a past difference in appearance. In this 르 irregular conjugation, 다르다 takes the past marker -았- and the statement ending -다 to become 달랐다.
The final -다 completes 달랐다 as a plain narrative statement about a past state.
는 marks Minister Hong as the person this statement is about.
을 marks his son as the person Minister Hong saw.
보고 connects seeing his son with being happy. The following past predicate places both in the past.
기뻤다 places Minister Hong's happiness in the past; 기쁘다 changes to 기뻤다.
The final 다 ends this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
이 marks Lady Yu as the subject of 낳은: she is the person who gave birth.
낳은 modifies 아들 and identifies a son whom Lady Yu had given birth to. The completed action is expressed by the modifier, without a separate past-tense suffix.
이 marks 아들 as the identity denied by 아니라서: Gildong was not a son born to Lady Yu.
아니라서 gives the reason Minister Hong also felt sad. Its past-time interpretation comes from the narrative and 있었다.
슬픈 describes 마음: sad feelings.
도 adds sadness to the happiness described immediately before this sentence: Minister Hong had sad feelings too.
The past marker in 있었다 places Minister Hong's sad feelings at this earlier point in the story.
The final -다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
은 establishes Gildong as the person whose growth and age are being narrated.
-아서 connects growing up with reaching eight years of age. The final past-tense predicate supplies past time for 자라서; this expresses a sequence of development.
이 marks 여덟 살 as the age Gildong reached; 여덟 살이 되었다 means he turned eight.
-었- places reaching this age in the past. 되었다 means 'turned' here.
-다 closes the past-tense predicate as a plain narrative statement.
His intelligence explains why learning one thing enabled him to understand many others. The final past predicate supplies the past time here.
를 marks one thing as what he learned.
면 describes a recurring situation: whenever he learned one thing. Its time is understood within the past narration.
도 adds other things to the one thing he learned explicitly.
알 is the modifier form of 알다 before 수; it contributes the action of knowing to the ability construction.
The complete construction expresses his ability to understand other things, with 있었다 placing that ability in the past.
었 places the ability expressed by 알 수 있다 in the past.
다 closes the past-tense predicate in the chapter's plain narrative register.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic; the sentence describes his affection for Gildong.
을 marks Gildong as the person Minister Hong loved.
사랑하다 becomes 사랑했다 with past -였-, contracted to 했, and the statement ending -다. The complete form means ‘loved’.
-다 ends this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
에게 identifies Gildong as the person who had words he could not use; it works with 있었다 rather than marking an action's recipient.
는 sets Gildong apart as the topic, introducing a restriction that applied to him.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수 to present calling someone as a possible action.
부를 수 없는 modifies 말: these were terms Gildong could not use to address his family members.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: that he could not use to address someone

grammar_links.context_en: 없는 modifies 말 as part of 부를 수 없는; the complete phrase describes words he could not use.
이 marks 말 as the subject of 있었다: such words existed for Gildong.
The past marker places the existence of this restriction in the narrative's past.
The ending 다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
를 marks his father as the person he could not address with the quoted title.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the title he could not use when addressing his father.
부를 modifies 수, presenting calling someone by a title as a possible action.
The complete negative construction says that Gildong could not call his own father ‘Father’ because his circumstances prohibited it.
The past marker in 없었다 places the impossibility of using that title in the past narrative.
The final 다 completes 없었다 as a plain narrative statement; within 부를 수 없었다, it states that calling him that was not possible.
도 adds Inhyeong to the family members Gildong could not address with an ordinary family title.
The copula identifies Inhyeong as Gildong's older brother.
The relationship is described within the past-time narrative.
Although Inhyeong was his older brother, Gildong could not call him “older brother.”
이라고 marks the quoted family title 형 as the name Gildong could not use when addressing Inhyeong.
부를 modifies 수, presenting calling someone as the action whose possibility is denied.
The whole construction expresses a restriction imposed on Gildong, rather than a lack of speaking ability.
The inability to use the family title held at this time in Gildong's childhood.
다 closes the past predicate in the chapter's plain narrative register.
그렇다 takes -게 to mean ‘that way’, referring to Gildong's use of the family titles. The written stem-final ㅎ remains in 그렇게.
Introduces the condition: whenever Gildong used those family titles, his father scolded him. The past narrative supplies the time of this repeated situation.
Makes Gildong's father the topic of the consequence: he was the one who scolded Gildong.
Marks Gildong as the person receiving the scolding. 길동 is the reviewed shortened name of 홍길동.
Places the scolding in the past narrative. 혼내었다 contracts to 혼냈다.
The ending -다 closes this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
의 connects Gildong to his mother: 'Gildong's mother'.
은 makes Chunseom, identified as Gildong's mother, the topic of the explanation.
이 marks social status as what was low.
-았- places Chunseom's low social standing in the story's past.
-기 nominalizes the past description so that it can supply the reason before 때문이다.
-기 때문이다 explains the preceding restriction: it was because Chunseom had low social status.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: is because her social status was low

grammar_links.context_en: 이다 completes 때문 as a predicate identifying the reason.
-다 closes the explanation in the chapter's plain narrative register.
에 marks the society in which the two groups existed.
는 follows 에 to establish that society as the setting and topic of the statement.
높은 modifies 신분: the status is high, rather than the people being physically tall.
의 connects 높은 신분 to 사람, describing people with high social status.
과 joins people of high status and people of low status; the subject marker on the second group applies to both.
낮은 modifies 신분, describing low social standing.
의 connects 낮은 신분 to 사람, describing people with low social status.
이 marks the coordinated groups of people as what existed in that society.
The past marking places the existence of these social groups in the story's past.
The final -다 closes the past statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
의 connects the mother to her social status: ‘the mother's social status’.
이 marks the mother's social status as the subject of ‘be low’ in the conditional clause.
낮으면 introduces the condition ‘if the mother's social status was low’. The past main clause supplies the historical time frame.
의 connects the child to the child's social status.
도 means ‘too’: the child's status was low just as the mother's was.
-았- places the child's low social standing in the historical setting of the story.
-다 ends this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
은 sets Gildong as the topic of the contrast between being Minister Hong's son and receiving unequal treatment.
의 links Minister Hong to his son.
The copula identifies Gildong as Minister Hong's son.
The past copula places this family relationship within the narrated past.
지만 contrasts his being Minister Hong's son with his inability to live on equal terms with Inhyeong.
의 identifies the social status as his mother's.
어머니의 신분 때문에 gives his mother's social status as the reason for the unequal treatment.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: because of his mother's social status

grammar_links.context_en: 과 marks Inhyeong as the person whose way of living Gildong could not share equally.
살 is the modifier form of 살다 before 수; the stem already ends in ㄹ, so its spelling remains 살.
The complete negative construction expresses that circumstances prevented Gildong from living in the same way as Inhyeong.
었 places the lack of possibility in the narrated past.
다 closes the sentence in the chapter's plain written narrative register.
은 makes Gildong the topic of the sentence.
이 marks the age expression 열 살 as what Gildong had exceeded.
었 places Gildong's being over ten in the past.
지만 contrasts his increased age with his continuing inability to use ordinary family titles.
와 joins his father and older brother; the object marker on 형 applies to both.
을 marks his father and older brother as the people he could not address that way.

그렇다 takes -게 to form 그렇게, meaning ‘that way’: addressing them as ‘father’ and ‘older brother.’ The written stem 그렇- retains ㅎ before -게. Pronunciation with an aspirated consonant does not alter this spelling.
지 connects 부르다 to 못하다, which supplies the meaning of inability.
The complete negative predicate says that Gildong was unable to address them with those family titles.
했 is the contracted past form of 하다 within the auxiliary 못하다.
다 closes the past auxiliary in the chapter's plain narrative register.
에서 marks the household as the place where these people worked.
일하는 modifies 사람들: the people who worked in the household. Their work belongs to the past situation described by the narration.
들 explicitly marks 사람 as plural, referring to the household workers.
까지 means ‘even’ here, emphasizing that the unequal treatment extended to the household workers too.
을 marks Gildong as the person the workers looked down on.
낮게 describes their judgment of Gildong's status. With 보았다, it means they looked down on him, rather than physically looking downward.
-았- makes 보았다 past tense. In 낮게 보았다, 보다 expresses a judgment: the workers looked down on Gildong.
The final -다 completes the past statement in plain narrative style. The whole expression 낮게 보았다 means ‘looked down on him’, describing contempt for Gildong's social status.
은 marks Gildong as the person whose feelings the sentence describes.
-고 connects Gildong's sadness with his emotional pain. The past tense of 아팠다 supplies the past-time interpretation for 슬프고 too.
이 marks 마음 as the subject of 아팠다. His heart hurting expresses emotional pain.
-았- places the emotional pain in the past. The stem 아프- loses ㅡ before -았-, producing 아팠-; with the statement ending -다, the complete form is 아팠다.
-다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative style.
The copula identifies the time of the scene as a night.
The past marker places this autumn night in the story's past.
The final -다 closes a plain narrative statement after the past-marked copula.
이 marks the moon as the subject: it was bright.
-았- places the moon's brightness at the past time of the scene.
-다 ends this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative style.
은 makes Gildong the topic of the narrated actions.
을 marks the written text as what Gildong was reading.
-다가 presents reading as the ongoing activity interrupted before Gildong pushed the desk and sighed. The final predicate supplies past time.
을 marks the desk as what Gildong pushed.
-고 joins pushing the desk to sighing. The final predicate supplies past time for both actions.
을 marks 한숨 as the object of 쉬다. Together, 한숨을 쉬었다 means that he let out a sigh.
-었- places the sigh in the past and supplies past time for the connected actions.
-다 closes the past-tense predicate in the plain narrative register.
는 marks Gildong, speaking as ‘I’, as the topic of his statement.
를 marks 나라 as the object of 위하다: the country whose interests he wants to serve.
나라를 위해 identifies whose benefit the desired work would serve: his country.
위하다 takes the connective form 위하여, contracted to 위해. In 나라를 위해, it means ‘for the sake of’ and modifies the following action.
중요한 describes the following noun 일 as important.
을 marks 일 as the work Gildong wants to do.
하고 links 하다 to 싶다; it does not mean ‘and’ between separate actions here.
하고 싶다 expresses Gildong's own wish to do important work.
The descriptive auxiliary 싶다 takes the plain statement ending -다 in Gildong's direct speech.
내 contracts 나의: the speaker refers to his own name.
을 marks 이름 as what the people would remember.
많은 modifies 사람들이, describing a large number of people.
들 explicitly marks 사람 as plural: people.
이 marks the people as those who would remember the speaker's name.
-면 presents people remembering his name as the imagined condition he hopes for.
-면 좋겠다 expresses his wish that many people remember his name for a long time.
In 좋겠다, -겠- expresses a desired outcome: it would be nice if people remembered his name.
-다 completes 좋겠다 as a plain statement expressing the speaker's wish.
는 marks the speaker as the topic: he wonders why he himself is alone.
이렇- takes -게 to form 이렇게, meaning ‘like this’; the written ㅎ remains. Here it describes Gildong's isolation despite having a father and brother.
The copula connects 혼자 to the speaker, expressing that he is alone.
-일까 makes this a question Gildong asks himself about his current loneliness, rather than a prediction about the future.
도 adds the father to the family members Gildong has: he has a father as well as an older brother.
있고 connects having a father with having an older brother. Both describe Gildong's present situation.
도 means 'too': Gildong also has an older brother.
있는데 contrasts having these relatives with being unable to address them by their family titles.
와 joins the two titles, 'father' and 'older brother', which the following quotation marker presents as forms of address.
이라고 marks the coordinated titles 아버지와 형 as the words Gildong cannot use to address his relatives.
-지 links 부르다 to 못하다; the inability comes from the following auxiliary.
부르지 못한다 expresses Gildong's inability to address his father and older brother by their ordinary family titles because of his social position.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: I cannot call them by those titles

grammar_links.context_en: 못한다 uses a present plain statement ending in Gildong's private speech about his current inability.
이 marks 마음 as what hurts. Gildong is describing his own emotional pain.
The descriptive predicate ends in plain -다 as Gildong states his present emotional pain. Its written form is identical to the dictionary headword.
은 marks Gildong as the topic of the narration.
을 marks his words as what he finishes; 말을 마치다 means to finish speaking.
-고 connects finishing speaking with going outside. The past tense of 나갔다 places both actions in the past.
으로 marks the direction of his movement: outside.
-았- places his going out in the past. 나가 combines with -았- by vowel contraction, and the complete statement is 나갔다.
-다 completes 나갔다 as a past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
에서 marks the yard as the place where Gildong practiced.
을 marks the sword as what Gildong used.
쓰는 modifies 연습: practice in using a sword. The modifier describes the activity practiced at that past time.
을 marks practice as the activity Gildong did; 연습을 했다 means he practiced.
했다 is the contracted past form of 하다 and places the practice in the past.
The final 다 ends the past statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
도 adds Minister Hong as another person who was outside.
에서 marks outside as the place where Minister Hong was looking at the moon.
을 marks the moon as what Minister Hong was looking at.
보고 links 보다 to the auxiliary 있다. The following 있었다 supplies the ongoing aspect and past narrative time, so here 보고 describes looking that was underway.
보고 있었다 describes looking at the moon as an action already in progress at this point in the story.
The past marking on the auxiliary places the ongoing looking in the past.
The final -다 closes the sentence in the chapter's plain narrative register.
는 makes Minister Hong, referred to as ‘he’, the topic.
을 marks Gildong as the person Minister Hong saw.
고 connects seeing Gildong with calling him over. The final past-tense predicate places both actions in the past.
부르다 takes the past marker with the 르 irregular change, yielding 불렀다: Minister Hong called Gildong over.
The ending 다 completes 불렀다 as a plain past-tense narrative statement.
이 marks 밤 as the subject of the description that the night has gotten late.
-게 turns 이렇다 into 이렇게, meaning ‘this’ in ‘this late’. The written stem-final ㅎ remains before -게; its pronunciation with ㄱ as [ㅋ] does not change the spelling.
었 presents the late hour as a state already reached: it has gotten late. The father is referring to the current late hour.
는데 follows the past marker and presents the late hour as background for the father's question about why Gildong is still awake.
을 marks 잠 as the object in 잠을 자다, the ordinary expression meaning to sleep.
안 negates 자. Together they ask whether he is not sleeping; with 왜 and 아직, the father asks why he is still not asleep.
The -아/어 ending contracts with 자- to give 자. Question intonation makes this a familiar, non-polite question from the father to his son.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
께 respectfully marks his father as the person receiving Gildong's answer.
했다 is the contracted past form of 하다 in 대답하다, placing the answer in the past.
The final 다 ends this past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
이 marks the moon as the subject of ‘was bright’.
The moon's brightness explains why Gildong was looking at it. The following past predicate supplies the past time.
-고 links 보다 to the ongoing-action auxiliary 있다; it does not mean ‘and’ here. 있었습니다 makes this looking ongoing at a past moment.
The complete phrase describes Gildong looking at the moon at that past moment, in respectful speech to his father.
-었- places the ongoing action of looking at the moon in the past.
-습니다 ends Gildong's statement formally and politely when addressing his father.
은 introduces people as the topic: the speaker makes a general statement about everyone's importance.
-지요 politely invites agreement that all people are important, establishing the premise for Gildong's following question.
는 marks the humble pronoun 저 as the topic: Gildong is asking about himself.
중요한 describes 사람: an important person.
이 on 사람이 marks the identity denied by 아닌: being an important person.
아닌 modifies 것, presenting the negative situation as something Gildong reflects on.
The entire negative clause precedes 것 같다. Gildong wonders why he seems not to count as an important person.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: might I seem not to be an important person?

grammar_links.context_en: -을까 expresses Gildong's wondering about why he seems unimportant, rather than a future action.
요 makes the reflective question polite when Gildong addresses his father.
는 marks Minister Hong as the topic: the sentence tells us what he understood.
의 identifies Gildong as the person whose words Minister Hong understood. 길동 is the approved shortened name for 홍길동.
을 marks Gildong's words as what Minister Hong understood.
했 is the contracted past form of 하다 within 이해하다, placing the understanding in the past.
다 closes the past-tense verb as a plain narrative statement.
을 marks Gildong as the person Minister Hong scolded.
-면서 shows that Minister Hong asked his question while scolding Gildong. The final past-tense predicate places both actions in the past.
묻다 changes its stem-final ㄷ to ㄹ before -었-, giving 물었다: he asked.
-다 closes the past-tense verb as a plain narrative statement.
그게 contracts 그것이. It marks Gildong's preceding statement as the subject of the father's question.
The copula attaches to 말, identifying what kind of statement the father is asking about.
After consonant-ending 말, -이야 gives a familiar, non-polite copular ending. Here question intonation makes it a direct question to his son.
무슨 asks what kind of remark is meant, and 말이야 supplies the informal copular question. Together the phrase asks the son to explain what he means.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: he bowed again and spoke.
에서 marks where Gildong bowed and spoke. 아버지 앞에서 means ‘in front of his father.’
을 marks 절 as the object of 하다. Together, 절을 하다 means ‘to bow,’ an act of respect.
하고 connects bowing to speaking. The past ending in 말했다 places both actions in the past.
말하였다 contracts to 말했다. The past marker presents his speaking as a completed event.
The final -다 closes the past statement in the chapter’s plain narrative register.
를 marks the speaker as the person his parents gave birth to and raised.
Connects giving birth to raising the child. Both actions are understood as completed before this expression of gratitude.
기르다 becomes 길러 through 르 irregular conjugation and connects to the benefactive auxiliary 주다. The completed time is understood from 주신 and the context.
길러 주신 describes the parents as having raised the speaker for his benefit. The honorific and completed-action modifier refer to those parents.
시 honors the parents who raised the speaker, rather than the recipient of their care.
The completed-action modifier makes the preceding action describe 부모님: the parents who raised him.
께 respectfully marks the parents as the people toward whom the speaker's gratitude is directed.
The formal polite ending expresses the speaker's gratitude respectfully.
는 marks Gildong's respectful self-reference 저 as the topic: 'As for me'.
의 connects 아버지 to 아들: Gildong is his father's son. He addresses his father directly, so natural English uses 'your son'.
The copula identifies Gildong as his father's son.
입니다 gives the noun-and-copula statement a formal polite ending as Gildong speaks respectfully to his father.
를 marks Gildong's father as the person he cannot address with the quoted family title.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the exact title Gildong cannot use when addressing his father.
-지 connects 부르다, ‘call or address’, to 못하다, which expresses inability.
Gildong cannot use the title because his social circumstances prevent it, rather than because he lacks the ability to speak.
-ㅂ니다 makes Gildong's statement to his father formally polite; it expresses his present inability.
저 takes possessive 의 to form 저의, meaning ‘my’ in respectful speech; 저의 contracts to 제. It identifies the older brother as the speaker's brother.
도 extends the same restriction to his older brother: he cannot use the ordinary family title for his brother either.
이라고 marks the quoted title ‘형’ as what he cannot call his older brother.
-지 connects 부르다 to 못하다, which supplies the inability; 부르지 alone does not express the negation.
부르지 못합니다 expresses that circumstances prevent him from calling his older brother ‘형’.
-ㅂ니다 makes 못하다 a formal polite statement addressed to his father.
이 marks this situation as what causes the speaker sadness.
-ㅂ니다 makes the statement formally polite as Gildong addresses his father.
도 adds Gildong to the category of people: ‘I too’.
The copula identifies Gildong as a person.
-인데 contrasts his being a person like everyone else with the painful life he must lead.
이렇다 takes -게 to describe the manner of living: ‘like this’. The written stem 이렇- retains ㅎ before -게, giving 이렇게. Its pronunciation [이러케] reflects aspiration of ㄱ after ㅎ, not a written stem change.
-아야 connects 살다 to 하다 to express necessity rather than a freely chosen way of living.
Gildong respectfully questions why he must live under these restrictions. 합니까 makes the necessity construction a formal polite question.
-ㅂ니까 ends Gildong's question to his father in a formal polite style.
은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
을 marks tears as what Gildong shed.
-었- places the shedding of tears in the past; 흘리었다 contracts to 흘렸다.
-다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
에 marks his tears as the cause of his clothes becoming wet.
이 marks his clothes as the subject of becoming wet.
-었- places the clothes becoming wet in the past.
-다 closes the past-tense statement in plain narrative style.
도 adds Minister Hong as someone who also felt sympathy for Gildong.
이 marks Gildong as the person who was pitiable in Minister Hong's eyes. Natural English expresses this as Minister Hong feeling sorry for him.
하다 combines with the past marker -였- and contracts to 했-. The complete form 불쌍했다 describes Minister Hong's sympathy for Gildong in the past.
-다 closes the past descriptive predicate as a plain narrative statement; it does not represent a change from informal speech.
에게 marks Gildong as the person to whom the kind words would be directed.
따뜻한 describes the words as kind and emotionally warm, rather than physically warm.

The verb clause modifies 것 to name an act. With 이, the entire act of saying kind words to Gildong becomes the subject of 걱정이었다. The sentence describes a contemplated act that worried his father, not an act already performed.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: saying kind words to him (as the subject)

grammar_links.context_en: 을 marks 말 as what would be said; 하다 here means to speak or say words.
하다 contracts to 해 and links to the benefactive auxiliary 주다.
해 주는 presents saying the words as an action done for Gildong's benefit. 주는 modifies 것 in the following tap.
주는 modifies 것, forming a reference to doing the preceding action for someone. This modifier does not assert that the contemplated action happened.
이 marks the nominalized act of saying kind words as the source of the father's worry.
The copula connects the contemplated act to 걱정, identifying it as a source of worry.
The past copular form places the father's worry at this point in the narrated past.
Final -다 closes the sentence in the chapter's plain written narrative register.
이 marks Gildong as the person who might forget his status.
을 marks social status as what Gildong might forget.
잊을 modifies 것 and presents forgetting as a possible later action, viewed from the father's past perspective.
잊을 것 같았다 expresses Minister Hong's impression that Gildong would probably forget his social status; it does not state that Gildong actually forgot it.
았 places the father's impression in the past; the possible forgetting was still later from that perspective.
다 closes the sentence in the chapter's plain narrative register.
으로 presents Gildong's social standing as the basis limiting what he can do; it does not indicate movement or classification.
할 modifies 수 to identify the action whose possibility is denied.
The negative ability construction modifies 일: things Gildong cannot do given his status.
없는 puts 없다 before 일, making the lack of possibility describe those things.
까지 emphasizes inclusion of even the things forbidden by Gildong's social standing.
하려고 links doing those things to an intention or attempt.
With auxiliary 하다, -려고 expresses an intention or attempt. Here Minister Hong anticipates that Gildong would try to act beyond his permitted position.
The auxiliary's 할 form modifies 것, presenting the attempt as an anticipated possibility.
The prospective clause with 것 같았다 expresses Minister Hong's past impression of what Gildong might attempt.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: seemed likely to try to do

grammar_links.context_en: The past marking locates Minister Hong's apprehension at that point in the narrative.
-다 closes the past predicate in the chapter's plain written narrative register.
큰 modifies 소리 to describe a loud voice.
로 marks the manner of scolding. 큰 소리로 means ‘in a loud voice’.
을 marks Gildong as the person Minister Hong scolded.
The past marker places the scolding in the past; 혼내었다 contracts to 혼냈다.
다 closes the past-tense statement in the chapter's plain narrative register.
높은 describes 사람 as having high social rank.
의 connects the high-ranking person to that person's household.
에서 marks the household where the woman works.
일하는 describes 여자 by her work in the household.
가 marks the woman as the subject of 낳은: she gave birth to the sons being described.
낳은 describes 아들 through the completed action of giving birth.
은 establishes these sons as the topic; the father says Gildong is not the only one.
너 말고도 means ‘besides you as well’: the father says other sons share Gildong's circumstances.
말고 follows 너 to mean ‘besides you’, referring to sons other than Gildong.
도 adds ‘as well’: other sons in these circumstances exist too.
있다 ends the father's assertion in a plain, non-polite style: there are other sons in the same circumstances.
도 means ‘too’: Minister Hong includes Gildong among sons born to women working in high-ranking households.
The copula identifies Gildong as that kind of son; it is incorporated into the connective form 아들인데.
-인데 presents Gildong's identity as background while contrasting it with his complaint: ‘You too are that kind of son, yet why …?’
을 marks 이런 말, ‘words like these’, as what Gildong says.
해 is the contracted 하여 form used as a non-polite question ending. Here 하다 means ‘say’, and Minister Hong asks his younger son why he says such things.
는 emphasizes ‘again’ in the prohibition: he must never say such things again.
을 marks these words as what Gildong is forbidden to say.
하지 connects 말하다's equivalent 말 하다 (‘say words’) to the negative auxiliary 말다, forming a prohibition.
하지 마라 is Minister Hong's direct command forbidding Gildong from saying such things.
마라 is the contracted plain command form of 말다; Minister Hong speaks sternly to his son.
을 marks 말을 as what Gildong would say.
하면 introduces the condition: if Gildong says such words again. Here 말을 하다 means to say words.
내 contracts 나의, meaning 'my'; Minister Hong refers to his own presence.
에 marks 앞 as the destination of coming: before Minister Hong, or into his presence.

beats.event_en: During King Sejong's reign, the respected Minister Hong has two sons: Inhyeong, born to his wife Lady Yu, and Gildong, born to the household servant Chunseom.
beats.quote: 화셜 됴션국 셰종됴 시졀의 ᄒᆞᆫ ᄌᆡ샹이 이시니 셩은 홍이오 명은 뫼라. ᄃᆡᄃᆡ 명문거죡으로 쇼년 등과ᄒᆞ여 벼ᄉᆞᆯ이 니죠판셔의 니르ᄆᆡ, 물망이 됴야의 읏듬이오, 츙효 겸비ᄒᆞ기로 일홈이 일국의 진동ᄒᆞ더라. 일즉 두 아들을 두어시니, 일ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆫ 일홈이 인형이니 뎡실 뉴시 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이오, 일ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆫ 일홈이 길동이니 시비 츈셤의 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이라.

beats.event_en: Chunseom becomes Minister Hong's concubine and gives birth to an extraordinary-looking boy. Hong is happy, but regrets that the child was not born to his wife.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 언파의 손을 ᄯᅥᆯ치고 나가거ᄂᆞᆯ, 공이 가쟝 무류ᄒᆞ여 분긔ᄅᆞᆯ ᄎᆞᆷ지 못ᄒᆞ고 외당의 나와 부인의 지식이 업스물 한탄ᄒᆞ더니, 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 시비 츈셤이 ᄎᆞᄅᆞᆯ 올니긔로 그 고요ᄒᆞ믈 인ᄒᆞ여 츈셤을 잇글고 협실의 드러가 졍이 친압ᄒᆞ니, 이 ᄯᆡ 츈셤의 나히 십팔이라. ᄒᆞᆫ 번 몸을 허ᄒᆞᆫ 후로 문외의 나지 아니ᄒᆞ고 타인을 ᄎᆔᄒᆞᆯ ᄯᅳᆺ이 업스니, 공이 긔특이 넉여 인ᄒᆞ여 잉쳡을 삼아더니, 과연 그 달붓허 ᄐᆡ긔 잇셔 십 삭만의 일ᄀᆡ 옥동을 ᄉᆡᆼᄒᆞ니, 긔골이 비범ᄒᆞ여 진짓 영웅 호걸의 긔상이라. 공이 일변 깃거ᄒᆞ나 부인의게 나지 못ᄒᆞ믈 한ᄒᆞ더라.

beats.event_en: By eight, Gildong learns remarkably quickly and his father treasures him. Nevertheless, his birth status prevents him from calling his father 'father' or his older brother 'older brother.' Even after ten, he remains unable to use these titles, and the servants' contempt causes him deep distress. One autumn night, he pushes aside his reading desk and sighs.

beats.event_en: Gildong wishes to accomplish great deeds for his country and make his name remembered. He laments his loneliness and the pain of having a father and brother whom he cannot address as family.
beats.quote: “대쟝뷔 셰샹의 나ᄆᆡ 공ᄆᆡᆼ을 본밧지 못ᄒᆞ면, 찰아리 병법을 외와 대쟝닌을 요하의 빗기 ᄎᆞ고 동졍셔벌ᄒᆞ여, 국가의 ᄃᆡ공을 셰우고 일홈을 만ᄃᆡ의 빗ᄂᆡ미 쟝부의 쾌ᄉᆡ라. 나ᄂᆞᆫ 엇지ᄒᆞ여 일신이 젹막ᄒᆞ고 부형이 이시되 호부호형을 못ᄒᆞ니 심쟝이 터질지라. 엇지 통한치 아니리오.”

beats.event_en: Gildong goes into the courtyard to practice swordsmanship. His father, who is also outside enjoying the moonlight, sees him and calls him over.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 말을 맛츠며 ᄯᅳᆯ의 나려 검술을 공부ᄒᆞ더니, 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 공이 ᄯᅩᄒᆞᆫ 월ᄉᆡᆨ을 구경ᄒᆞ다가 길동의 ᄇᆡ회ᄒᆞ믈 보고 즉시 불너 문왈,

beats.event_en: Minister Hong asks why Gildong is still awake so late.
beats.quote: “네 무ᄉᆞᆷ 흥이 이셔 야심토록 잠을 ᄌᆞ지 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ다?”

beats.event_en: Gildong says he enjoys the moonlight, but explains that although people are supposed to be precious, he feels that he himself is treated as having no worth.
beats.quote: “쇼인이 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 월ᄉᆡᆨ을 사랑ᄒᆞ미여니와, 대개 하ᄂᆞᆯ이 만물을 ᄂᆡ시ᄆᆡ 오직 사ᄅᆞᆷ이 귀ᄒᆞ오나, 쇼인의게 니ᄅᆞ러ᄂᆞᆫ 귀ᄒᆞ오미 업ᄉᆞ오니 엇지 사ᄅᆞᆷ이라 ᄒᆞ오리잇가.”

beats.event_en: Minister Hong understands what Gildong means but deliberately responds reproachfully.

beats.event_en: Minister Hong asks what Gildong means.
Gildong explains that he is grateful to his parents, yet his lifelong sorrow is being forbidden to call his own father 'father' and his own brother 'older brother.'
beats.quote: “쇼인이 평ᄉᆡᆼ 셜운 바ᄂᆞᆫ, 대감 졍긔로 당당ᄒᆞ온 남ᄌᆡ 되여ᄉᆞ오니 부ᄉᆡᆼ모휵지은이 깁ᄉᆞᆸ거ᄂᆞᆯ, 그 부친을 부친이라 못ᄒᆞ옵고, 그 형을 형이라 못ᄒᆞ오니 엇지 사ᄅᆞᆷ이라 ᄒᆞ오리잇가.”

beats.event_en: Gildong cries. His father feels pity, but fears that comforting him would encourage him to overstep his assigned position, so he scolds him harshly.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 눈물을 흘여 단삼을 젹시거ᄂᆞᆯ, 공니 쳥파의 비록 측은ᄒᆞ나 만일 그 ᄯᅳᆺ을 위로ᄒᆞ면 ᄆᆞᄅᆞᆷ이 방ᄌᆞᄒᆞᆯ가 져어 크게 ᄭᅮ지져 왈,

beats.event_en: Minister Hong says Gildong is not the only child born to a servant in an official's household and warns him never to raise the matter again.
beats.quote: “ᄌᆡ샹가 쳔비 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이 비단 너ᄲᅮᆫ이 아니거든, 네 엇지 방ᄌᆞᄒᆞ미 이 ᄀᆞᆺ흐뇨. ᄎᆞ후 다시 이런 말이 이시면 안젼의 용납지 못ᄒᆞ리라.”

beats.event_en: Gildong cannot answer and can only bow down and cry. His father orders him to leave, and Gildong returns to his room, still grieving.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ니, 길동이 감이 일언을 고치 못ᄒᆞ고 다만 복지유쳬 ᄲᅮᆫ이라. 공이 명ᄒᆞ여 물너가라 하거ᄂᆞᆯ, 길동이 침쇼로 도라와 슬허ᄒᆞ믈 마지 아이ᄒᆞ더라.

bindings.analysis_en: 위해 is explicitly contained in 을/를 위해; it is not sentence-final -어.
bindings.optional_reason_en: One internal linking form belongs to the same country-service phrase and adds no separate unfamiliar construction.
One common wish expresses wanting his name remembered; its conditional clause uses familiar Level 2 formation.

bindings.analysis_en: Desiderative -겠- in 좋겠다; the complete wish construction is separately bound.
Reflective questions, including polite related forms; future reference is not required.
Background and contrast, including copular and past-marked forms.

The grammar catalog has no matching 안 + predicate construction. Vocabulary source nikl2017-vocabulary-00417 establishes the negative adverb's identity and meaning, but does not provide grammar evidence for this construction. -지 않다 is a different formation.
bindings.optional_reason_en: One short 안 자 question uses a common negative adverb before the familiar sleep verb. The late-night setting and 왜 아직 make the meaning clear; catalog absence does not make this simple question advanced.

bindings.analysis_en: Respectful 요 attached to the reflective question; complete -을까요 is also listed in its question-ending source.
bindings.optional_reason_en: One occurrence isolates politeness within an already familiar question form and adds no clause structure.

bindings.analysis_en: Copula 이다 plus informal -아/어 yields 이야/야; emphatic particle 이야 has a different identity.
Auxiliary-linking -아/어 is included in the benefactive constructions used here.
Honors the parents performing the raising action.
Linking -아야 is contained in the necessity construction; standalone prerequisite-condition -어야 is a different lesson.
Necessity with 하다 explicitly listed as a synonymous form.
Causal 에 marks tears as causing wet clothes; the particle row states no narrower function restriction.
Names the contemplated act of saying kind words.
으로 marks the basis or circumstances for possible action; distinct from capacity particle 으로서.
Intentional connective, distinct from sentence-final suspicion -려고2.

Intentional -려고 is listed, but its auxiliary 하다 construction expressing intention or attempt is not explicitly cataloged. The connective alone does not establish the auxiliary function; 하다01/보 consequently also remains unlisted.
bindings.optional_reason_en: One common intention construction expresses the father's fear. Embedding under 것 같았다 creates the hardest clause; sentence help and surrounding statements support the anticipated overstepping.

bindings.analysis_en: Noun exclusion 말고 is absent. Prohibitive -지 말다 does not cover this noun-following function.
bindings.optional_reason_en: One 너 말고도 phrase has two annotation links and means besides you as well. The sentence establishes that other sons share his circumstances.

bindings.analysis_en: Prohibition; the plain imperative ending is separately bound.
Direct plain commands, including contracted 마라 and 가라.
bindings.optional_reason_en: Two short stern commands distinguish the father's speech from respectful replies; their actions and prohibition are easy to identify.

bindings.analysis_en: Prospective modifier, dependent 것 and identifying copula form predictive 것이다. The imperative -을 것1 row does not establish this predictive function.
